problem_signature.question: In Seregin's logarithmic Type-II Euler scaling f(lambda)=ln(e/lambda)^(-gamma), characterize exactly which admissible moving radii a(lambda) make F_lambda=f(lambda a)/f(lambda) produce genuine smallness in unweighted scale-normalized A,E,D, and determine whether the source's fixed-radius compactness transfers that smallness to the ancient Euler limit.
problem_signature.lane: Type-II Euler-scaling / prelimit annular-tightness / local-to-global gluing

primary_sources.citation: G. Seregin, On potential Type II blowups for the Navier-Stokes equations, arXiv:2606.29468v1, 28 Jun 2026

source_signature.producer: suitable weak Navier-Stokes solution in Q obeying weighted local bounds
source_signature.rescaling: v^lambda=lambda f(lambda) v; q^lambda=lambda^2 f(lambda)^2 q; t=lambda^2 f(lambda) tau
source_signature.scaled_equation: partial_tau v^lambda + v^lambda·grad v^lambda - f(lambda) Delta v^lambda + grad q^lambda = 0
source_signature.limit: ancient Euler state on Q_- under fixed-radius local compactness
source_signature.critical_quantifier: source convergence is stated for every fixed a>0, not for a=a_k->infinity

hard_falsifiers: claimed gain at fixed-power interior radii without divergence of F_lambda
moving-radius gain silently passed through fixed-radius convergence
dimensionless smallness silently upgraded to absolute tail/flux tightness
uniform Navier-Stokes epsilon-regularity invoked after viscosity coefficient f(lambda)->0 without a source-valid uniform theorem
pressure/nonlocal and signed-flux residuals silently dropped
same-context review counted as independent review
